blocks.text: THE PROPHET GAD, “DAVID’S SEER” · UNITED KINGDOM
Gad. Counsel in the hold, three choices after the census, and an altar on a threshing floor.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophet
ERA
United kingdom c. 1050–930 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
David
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
The word came to him as a message to carry: “the word of the LORD came unto the prophet Gad, David’s seer, saying, Go and say unto David”.
THE CALL
How the word came
The word came to him as a message to carry: “the word of the LORD came unto the prophet Gad, David’s seer, saying, Go and say unto David”. 2 Samuel 24:11–12

Chronicles tells the same scene as “the LORD spake unto Gad, David’s seer”, and says that for the altar “the angel of the LORD commanded Gad to say to David” where to build it. 1 Chronicles 21:9 1 Chronicles 21:18
Chronicles names a written record: the acts of David are “written in the book of Samuel the seer, and in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the book of Gad the seer”. 1 Chronicles 29:29
It also names him as one of those whose commandment ordered the temple music: “for so was the commandment of the LORD by his prophets”. 2 Chronicles 29:25

HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS

From the textScripture does not tell how Gad's life ended. After the census story he is named only as the writer of a book of David's acts and, in Hezekiah's day, as one whose commandment had ordered the temple music. 1 Chronicles 29:29 2 Chronicles 29:25
TRADITION SAYS

Among the antiquities of Hebron the Jewish Encyclopedia lists “the tombs of Gad, Nathan the prophet, Abner”.[45] Who says so: A local tradition at Hebron, listed in the Jewish Encyclopedia, reported 1904; its earliest source has not been identified
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Three is the original number
A. F. Kirkpatrick (1881); the Pulpit Commentary (1880–1897); Ellicott's commentary (c. 1878–1884)

The Greek Septuagint also reads “three years” in 2 Samuel (Brenton's translation), and three fits the three months and three days. Kirkpatrick calls the reading of the Septuagint and Chronicles “unquestionably to be preferred”; the Pulpit Commentary says three is “probably right”. 2 Samuel 24:13 1 Chronicles 21:12 [72][98][18][7]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 5
1 Samuel 22 2 Samuel 24 1 Chronicles 21 1 Chronicles 29 2 Chronicles 29
PASSAGES · 5
1 Samuel 22:5 2 Samuel 24:11–19 1 Chronicles 21:9–19 1 Chronicles 29:29 2 Chronicles 29:25
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture gives no father, tribe or home for Gad.
It does not say when or how he became “David’s seer”.
The “book of Gad the seer” (1 Chronicles 29:29) is not among the books of the Bible; whether any of it survives in Samuel is a question above.
2 Samuel 24:19 says David went up “according to the saying of Gad”; neither account says what became of Gad afterwards.
